headline_fact: Wi-Fi connects your device to a local network; reaching a website needs a wider path.
summary: Follow a page request from a phone through a home router and towards a remote service.
did_you_know: A working local connection does not establish that every remote service is reachable.
core_mechanics: A local radio link carries data between a device and an access point. Other network links carry it onwards.
why_it_matters: Separating the local link from the wider path helps explain everyday connection problems.

in_depth_breakdown.real_world_application: A trolley carrying more mass needs more net force to achieve the same acceleration.

learning_takeaways: Separate the local wireless link from the wider network path.
One connection indicator does not describe the whole system.

share_text: Discover the difference between Wi-Fi and the wider internet path.

technology_lesson.hook: Wi-Fi connects your device to a local network; reaching a website needs a wider path.
technology_lesson.question: Why can Wi-Fi be connected while a website still does not open?
technology_lesson.learning_goal: Follow the local link and the wider network path as separate parts of one familiar experience.

opening_scenario.title: A connected symbol, but no page
opening_scenario.experience: You open a browser and request a page. The device shows a Wi-Fi connection, but the page is not available. The symbol tells you something about one part of the path, not every part.
opening_scenario.question: Which part of the connection does the symbol describe?

problem.what_is_hard: A remote page depends on several systems working together. A single connection indicator cannot explain the state of the whole path.
problem.why_it_matters: Separating those responsibilities makes the technology easier to understand without treating one symptom as a complete diagnosis.

technology_lesson.central_idea: A local radio link carries data between a device and an access point. Other network links carry it onwards.

inputs.name: Page request
inputs.explanation: A request for content from a remote service.

components.name: Your phone
components.role: The browser prepares a request. The device exchanges data over its local wireless connection.

components.name: Home router
components.role: A typical home device combines a Wi-Fi access point, which connects local wireless devices, with routing functions that send traffic onwards.

components.name: Remote service
components.role: A remote system handles the request and sends response data back through the network.

outputs.name: Returned page data
outputs.explanation: Response data that the browser can use to present the requested content.

walkthrough.title: The device prepares a request
walkthrough.what_happens: The browser asks for remote content, and the device prepares data to send through its network connection.
walkthrough.what_changes: A user action becomes data that the network can carry.

walkthrough.title: The local wireless link carries data
walkthrough.what_happens: The phone exchanges data with the home access point using radio signals. This is the local Wi-Fi part of the example.
walkthrough.what_changes: The request moves from the device into the local network.

walkthrough.title: The wider network path matters too
walkthrough.what_happens: Other network equipment carries the request onwards. A remote service can return data along a network path. The browser still depends on that wider exchange.
walkthrough.what_changes: The local request can become a remote exchange, followed by returned data.

diagram.title: One request, two different parts of the path
diagram.caption: A simplified path. The local radio link and the wider network exchange have different responsibilities.
diagram.description: The phone exchanges data with a home router over a local radio link. Other networks connect the home network with a remote service. Return arrows show that data also comes back.
assumptions: Other network equipment is omitted from this overview.
The home device combines an access point with routing functions.

worked_example.title: A page request in a home network
starting_conditions: The phone has joined the home wireless network.
The example uses a remote page rather than a local file.
actions: The browser requests content from the remote service.
The phone exchanges request data over its local Wi-Fi link.
The home network and other systems carry data onwards if the required path is available.
worked_example.outcome: The local wireless exchange can work even when the requested remote content is unavailable.
worked_example.explanation: The connection indicator concerns one part of the system. It does not establish that the remote service, name lookup and every intervening network link work.
limits: This example does not diagnose a particular device or reproduce a real request.
Real network paths contain more equipment and protocols than this overview shows.

tradeoffs.cost: A radio link depends on conditions such as distance, obstacles and competing use.
tradeoffs.when_it_matters: The same device can behave differently in different parts of a home.

failure_modes.symptom: Connected to Wi-Fi, but remote content is unavailable
failure_modes.cause: One possibility is that the local link works while some other part of the path is unavailable.
failure_modes.what_it_shows: The symptom alone does not identify the failed component.

practical_implications.title: Read indicators within their scope
practical_implications.explanation: A local connection indicator and the availability of a remote page describe different parts of the experience. Understanding that distinction helps you ask a more precise question.

misconceptions.belief: Wi-Fi and the internet mean the same connection
misconceptions.correction: Wi-Fi describes a local wireless connection; the wider network path is a separate part of the system.
misconceptions.explanation: A device can exchange data locally without establishing that a remote internet service is reachable.

optional_depth.title: What the radio link carries
optional_depth.explanation: Data is represented through changes in a radio signal. The exact methods depend on the wireless standard and equipment; this lesson does not model those details.

knowledge_checks.question: Does a Wi-Fi connection prove that a remote website is available?
knowledge_checks.answer: No. It describes a local connection, not the complete remote path.
knowledge_checks.explanation: The remote exchange depends on other systems beyond the local radio link.

takeaways: Separate the local wireless link from the wider network path.
One connection indicator does not describe the whole system.
